title: Delegated Approval, Escalation & Attestation Flow — PRD Draft
content:
SUMMARY
This PRD sketch outlines a delegated-approval and escalation framework for customer-managed networking on Private deployments. It combines: (1) a compact approval matrix for customer-operator interactions, (2) an attestation handshake pattern and evidence artifacts that must be appended to approval events, and (3) audit-log retention and search primitives so security/compliance teams can prove correct approval flows.

Problem statement
- Customers deploying Redwood Private often want the ability to delegate routine network changes (eg. port updates, CIDR revocations, peering) to operator teams while retaining an auditable, policy-governed approval surface.
- Current proposals focus on static approval gates or heavy manual handoffs; neither scales for frequent changes nor satisfies SOC/ISO auditors who ask for cryptographic attestations or policy-derived evidence.

Goals
- Provide a minimal, extensible delegated approval model that supports: direct approvals, role-based delegation, time-limited approvals, and automatic escalation when SLAs are missed.
- Attach verifiable attestation artifacts to each approval event (signed metadata, requester certificate, short-lived token provenance).
- Emit structured audit logs with queryable fields for: requestor_id, delegate_id, approval_policy_id, attestation_blob_id, decision, TTL, escalation_path.
- Offer retention and export controls that map to customer compliance needs (90/365/999 days) and support rolling evidence exports for audits.

Non-goals
- This draft does NOT attempt to replace the full customer IAM system or integrate with every enterprise IdP. We will rely on tokenized identities and a small connector surface for SAML/OIDC integration.
- Not addressing complete RBAC overhaul for the entire Console — scoped to networking/operator approvals.

User personas and example flows
1) Networking operator (delegate): routine request to rotate a BGP peer key.
   - Operator submits change via Console or CLI.
   - System checks active delegation policies; if permitted, creates a pending approval event with embedded attestation requirements (eg. operator signature + change diff).
   - Operator signs locally with short-lived key; console uploads attestation_blob and advances decision automatically if policy satisfied.

2) Customer security reviewer (owner): requires human review for cross-AZ peering change.
   - A formal approval is created; because of policy high-sensitivity flag, the system notifies reviewer(s) and opens a timed window (48h) for manual sign-off.
   - If reviewer does not respond, auto-escalate to the customer admin escalation list and record the escalation event.

3) Emergency rollback scenario: automated reversal triggered by safety monitor.
   - Safety monitor (system principal) triggers rollback. Approval event is created with reason and linked to monitoring alert id; attestation records the rollback author as "system" with alert id metadata.

Requirements (product & UX)
- Approval Matrix UI: compact view showing request, policy match, required attestations, current decision state, TTL, and escalation chain.
- Delegation builder: allow customer admin to define delegation bundles (eg. network-ops team can approve port/CIDR edits under 24h TTL up to /23 scope).
- Escalation policy editor: list of escalation targets with order, timeouts, and contact channels (email, Slack webhook, PagerDuty).
- Attestation capture: Console and CLI must accept an attestation_blob (base64) plus an optional signer_cert_id. UI shows a human-readable summary of the attestation for reviewers.
- Structured audit log schema (minimum fields): event_id, timestamp, requestor_id, delegate_id, target_resource, action, decision, policy_id, attestation_blob_id, escalation_events[], retention_tier.
- Search/export endpoints: allow filtering by policy_id, requestor_id, time-window, decision, or attestation_blob_id. Export in ndjson for downstream SIEM ingest.

Requirements (backend & infra)
- Approvals service: low-latency event store for approval events with append-only semantics and immutability guarantees (WORM flag for retention).
- Attestation store: S3-like object store with content-addressable IDs and optional server-side encryption customer key option.
- Signatures: support RSA/ECDSA verification for uploaded attestations and support verification chain metadata in logs.
- Retention policy enforcement: background job to apply retention tiers and produce compliant exports on demand.

Telemetry & Observability
- Per-route metrics: approval throughput, avg time-to-decision, escalation frequency, fallback rates.
- Audit integrity hooks: periodic sampling job that verifies attestation blobs against stored verification metadata and reports mismatches as alerts.
- Console dashboard: quick filters for "open approvals >24h", "escalated in last 7d", "failed attestation verifications".

API/contract: (sketch)
- POST /v1/private/approvals -> create approval event (payload: requester_id, target_resource, action, attachments[], required_attestations[], ttl_seconds, policy_hint)
- GET /v1/private/approvals/{id} -> fetch approval state (includes attestation_blob_ids, escalation_log)
- POST /v1/private/approvals/{id}/attest -> submit attestation (payload: signer_id, attestation_blob, signature_meta)
- POST /v1/private/approvals/{id}/decision -> make decision (auto or manual) with required signer info
- GET /v1/private/audit/export -> trigger export job (query params: from, to, policy_id, format=ndjson)

Security & Compliance notes
- All approval events must be signed by a recognized principal. For delegated operators with no PKI, we allow short-lived signed tokens issued by the customer's IdP connector; tokens are recorded with token_issuer metadata.
- WORM-enabled retention for audit evidence for customer-specified periods. Customers can request cryptographic proof-of-immutability for given time windows (HMAC chain; see infra design doc).
- Privacy: redact PII from audit exports by default; allow customers to opt-in to unredacted exports when required for incident response.

Rollout plan & milestones (proposal)
- Phase 0 (MVP, 8 weeks): Approval event model + UI, basic delegation builder, attestation accept API, short-lived token path, ndjson exports.
- Phase 1 (12 weeks): Escalation editor, escalation channels (Slack/PagerDuty integration), retention tiers, basic attestation verification job.
- Phase 2 (8 weeks): WORM retention, HMAC chaining proofs, customer-managed SSE-KMS for attestation store, audit export automation with scheduler.

Open questions / decisions to make
- Attestation format: use tokio-signed JSON vs cms/pkcs7? Tradeoffs: interoperability vs implementation complexity.
- Who runs the verification roots? Default Redwood trust bundle vs customer-supplied root. Need legal input on burden for enterprise customers.
- Do we require mandatory hardware-backed keys for high-sensitivity policies? How do we operationalize bring-your-own-HSM signing?

Action items / TODOs
- [ ] Engineering: prototype attestation_blob upload + verification service (owners: Carlos, Evan)
- [ ] Security: propose default trust bundle and attacker model (owner: Jules)
- [ ] Product: finalize policy DSL for delegation intensity (owner: Priya)
- [ ] Solutions Eng: map common customer workflows and build 3 example templates for delegation (owner: Ayesha)

Notes-to-self / loose thoughts
- Might surface "approval dry-run" where a requested change is evaluated against policy with simulated attestation requirements; helpful for onboarding.
- Could piggyback on the existing telemetry export pipeline for ndjson to SIEM to reduce infra lift.
- Consider an "audit passport" artifact that bundles a sequence of approval events + attestations for a single deployment change; useful for audits and support handoffs.

References / related artifacts
- jira:PRD-458 (product roadmap ticket)
- confluence:private-deploy-attestation-design-v2
- github:PR/207 (attestation prototype)

-- end of draft --

(Author note: this is intentionally pragmatic and scoped. Expect follow-ups to iterate on attestation schemas and the exact fields we publish into audit logs. Feedback wanted on the TTL/escalation defaults and on the attestation format choice.)
